candidates.title: Diffusion-enhanced GFlowNet for solving vehicle routing problems
candidates.abstract: Traditional neural solvers for solving vehicle routing problems (VRPs) often suffer from limited solution diversity, motivating the development of Generative Flow Network (GFlowNet)-based models.However, the effectiveness of these models is frequently constrained by insufficient flow expansion in high-reward regions, limiting their ability to distribute probability across promising solution routes.The deeper exploration could yield superior results.Diffusion models, in contrast, provide stronger structural guidance for exploration.These two paradigms are naturally complementary: GFlowNet can supply edge-level signals for diffusion to embed, while diffusion can guide broader exploration.Leveraging this synergy, we propose Diffusion-Enhanced GFlowNet (DEG), a novel framework that integrates GFlowNet with a diffusion model to encourage richer flow expansion toward highreward regions and derive higher-quality solutions.Specifically, DEG exploits GFlowNet's inherent diversity to generate edge-specific backward signals, applies the stochastic noise schedule of diffusion to perturb these signals, and then denoises them within the GFlowNet paradigm.To further improve scalability, we introduce a specialized decoder capable of dynamically adapting to diverse problem scales.Extensive experimental evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets, including instances with up to 10,000 nodes, demonstrate that DEG consistently achieves favorable performance compared to baseline methods.The code is available at https://github.com/ZHANG-NI/DEG.Recent neural solvers for VRPs can be broadly categorized into Autoregressive (AR) and Non-Autoregressive (NAR) models.AR models, such as those based on pointer networks and Transformer 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026).

candidates.title: Optimal-transport flow matching for stochastic model ipdating
candidates.abstract: Deep generative models have attracted considerable attention as inference engines for stochastic model updating. Among these deep generative models, conditional flow matching offers a particularly efficient formulation, in which a continuous transport map from a latent distribution to the posterior is learned by regression against optimal-transport probability paths, avoiding both the invertibility constraints of normalising flows and the iterative denoising of diffusion models. However, its performance in engineering model updating has not been examined against an established baseline such as the Bayesian updating framework under controlled conditions. In this work, conditional flow matching is therefore assessed against the Bayesian model updating approach with transitional Markov chain Monte Carlo, in which the Bhattacharyya distance provides the approximate likelihood for the Bayesian approach. The two methods are assessed with respect to posterior fidelity, evaluated by statistical distances against the known ground truth and computational expenditure in model evaluations, with the offline training budget reported separately from the inference cost of each subsequent conditioning. A 3-DOF spring–mass system with uncertain stiffness parameters serves as the benchmark. Since the calibrated posterior constitutes the input description upon which subsequent reliability assessment depends, the accuracy and the marginal cost of the updating step both bear directly on reliability computations. In addition, the amortised nature of the learned transport map is discussed in this work, as it permits the posterior to be re-evaluated under new observations at negligible cost, which is a property of practical relevance to reliability assessment under sequentially acquired monitoring data.

candidates.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
candidates.abstract: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. To investigate automated ranking, we introduce PyriteRep, a structured representation of molecular geometry, protein-ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores, and develop two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner, which directly compares poses through text-based reasoning, and PyriteFeaturizer, which generates executable code to construct features for logistic regression, optionally incorporating features derived from LLM subcalls. These agents achieve up to 67% and 74% accuracy, respectively, exceeding observed expert performance. LLM-guided feature discovery generally outperforms direct reasoning, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) improves open-weight models, enabling them to match or surpass closed-source frontier models in our evaluations. These results establish Pyrite as a challenging test of pose-ranking ability and highlight LLM-guided feature discovery as a promising approach to interpret and combine the outputs of computational chemistry tools.

candidates.title: Design of a multi-stage hybrid optimizer combining Bayesian and evolutionary algorithms for modeling and optimizing seizure-related information in EEG signals
candidates.abstract: The prediction of epileptic seizures from EEG signal analysis is modeled as a complex, high-dimensional, multi-objective optimization problem. In this study, we propose and design a novel multi-stage hybrid optimizer that integrates Bayesian optimization with a family of evolutionary and metaheuristic algorithms, including Genetic Algorithm (GA), Evolutionary Programming (EP), Evolution Strategies (ES), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), and Harmony Search (HS).This optimizer is structured to operate across sequential stages of optimization, where each stage is designed to progressively refine the solution space by selecting the optimal subset of EEG channels and time blocks related to the preictal phase. The mathematical model aims to maximize the posterior probability of seizure occurrence while minimizing the temporal distance to the actual seizure, thus formulating a well-defined trade-off in the objective space. Unlike traditional methods, the proposed hybrid framework models and controls the optimization trajectory by combining the global exploration capability of evolutionary algorithms with the adaptive search of Bayesian optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimizer successfully converges toward high-informational regions of EEG data that occur early in the preictal phase. A detailed performance comparison and sensitivity analysis further validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach, offering insights into the design of more generalizable hybrid optimizers for complex modeling tasks.

candidates.title: Survival of the fittest tool: choosing between open and closed artificial intelligence in pharmaceutical science
candidates.abstract: Three years ago, this journal published the editorial Technological Darwinism , urging pharmaceutical scientists to adapt to artificial intelligence (AI) rather than resist it. Since then, the question has shifted from whether to use AI to which AI to use, under what circumstances, and with what evidence. This review addresses that question by mapping current AI tools across the five canonical stages of drug development, from discovery to post-market pharmacovigilance. It is a narrative review, not a systematic one, and it treats openness as a spectrum rather than a binary. It compares two broad categories: open systems free, often open source or open weight, inspectable, and locally deployable and closed systems, which are proprietary, commercial, and delivered as a service. The central conclusion is pragmatic. For routine laboratory, educational, and research tasks, capable open tools now exist for almost every application, including manuscript drafting, literature review, reference management, statistical analysis, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modelling, calibration and standard-curve fitting, chemical structure drawing and SMILES handling, image and figure generation, and prediction of physicochemical, ADMET (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity), formulation, and excipient compatibility properties. Free web services, however, may require confidential structures to be uploaded to a third party, so openness is distinguished here from private deployment, and independent head to head evidence against commercial tools is uneven. In contrast, integrated end to end drug discovery and validated regulatory workflows remain dominated by proprietary platforms. During the period covered by this review, the first generative AI-designed molecule targeting a generative AI-derived protein reported positive Phase IIa results and entered Phase III in July 2026; protein structure prediction was recognized with the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, shared by Hassabis, Jumper and Baker and became partly open; an autonomous frontier language model improved a longstanding medicinal chemistry reaction through thousands of wet-laboratory experiments; and regulatory agencies issued their first guidance on AI credibility. The review argues that the most enduring competency is not mastery of any single AI platform but the ability to select appropriate tools, critically validate their outputs, and document their credibility in proportion to the decisions they inform. Accordingly, open AI systems should be the default for routine, low-risk, and educational applications, whereas proprietary platforms currently retain advantages for integrated discovery and regulated development. Credibility is defined operationally, human oversight is treated as a condition of use, and the review states where comparative evidence is lacking.

candidates.title: Diff-ANO: Towards fast high-resolution ultrasound computed tomography via conditional consistency models and adjoint neural operators
candidates.abstract: Abstract Ultrasound computed tomography (USCT) reconstructs sound speed from incomplete, noisy scattered-wave measurements. Its instability arises from the nonlinear inverse map and acquisition geometry. Generative models can supply learned priors that stabilize such partial differential equation (PDE)-constrained inversions. In this work, we introduce Diff-ANO (Diffusion-based models with adjoint neural operators), which alternates conditional consistency model (CM) refinement with surrogate measurement-gradient optimization. One forward multigrid neural operator (MgNO) predicts the transmitter/receiver source-field bank; a conjugated residual combination of those fields then forms the adjoint action and sound-speed gradient. Across four acquisition geometries, our method delivers strong reconstruction quality with a 6.75×online speedup over solver-based refinement in a matched computational-efficiency comparison. Independent finer-grid WaveSim measurements reduce potential convergent Born series (CBS) inverse crime and yield reconstruction trends consistent with the matched-CBS study. Together with additional evaluations of intermediate refinements and ablations, these results support efficient data-informed, measurement-guided USCT reconstruction and motivate extension to more realistic acquisition physics and measured data.

candidates.title: From Generative Molecular Design to Agentic Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery.
candidates.abstract: Over the past decade, artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly influenced the early stages of drug discovery, which focus primarily on target evaluation and the design or identification of new active small molecules or biologics. Deep neural networks adapted from areas such as natural language processing and computer vision have provided novel opportunities for generative modeling and human-machine interactions. State-of-the-art AI models for generative molecular design have emerged, but remain only little understood so far. Furthermore, new computational systems are being devised rapidly that are expected to significantly transform the drug discovery landscape in the near future. These developments pose challenges to computer-aided drug discovery in various ways. In the following, we discuss these opportunities and challenges, with a focus on molecular design.

candidates.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
candidates.abstract: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. This demonstrates that loss-based scaling laws alone are insufficient to predict when zero-shot emergent capabilities become available. The capabilities reported here emerge after training at a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio to accommodate the sparsity of paired biological interaction data. The same frozen representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods. In prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets spanning seven protein families, Bonbon achieves a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, yielding structurally novel molecules not previously reported to inhibit these proteins, including for out-of-distribution targets.

candidates.title: CLNA: controllable latent space of non-prompt attributes for enhancing diversity in text-to-image synthesis
candidates.abstract: Text-to-image synthesis in medicine remains challenging because clinically relevant visual attributes are often not fully specified by text prompts, which can limit the controllability and diversity of generated images. We propose Controllable Latent Space of Non-Prompt Attributes (CLNA), a framework that models non-prompt visual attributes within a continuous latent space for diagnosis-conditioned image synthesis, implemented with a style encoder and dual cross-attention within a Stable Diffusion backbone. We evaluated CLNA on otoendoscopic image synthesis for three diagnostic classes: normal tympanic membrane, otitis media with effusion, and chronic otitis media. Compared with the baseline Stable Diffusion model, CLNA improved image fidelity in the domain-adapted feature space, reducing Fréchet Inception Distance from 52.91 to 10.11 against the held-out internal test set, and improved feature-space recall from 57.67% to 90.22%. In classification experiments, replacing 10–40% of the real training data with CLNA-generated images at $$\:\gamma\:=0.5$$ gave F1 scores of 93.57–94.08% on the internal test set (vs. 94.46% averaged across 10 real-only runs) and 84.81–85.30% on the external test set (vs. 83.76% from a single real-only run). With complete replacement of the training data by generated images, CLNA outperformed the baseline model on both the internal test set (78.53% vs. 70.25%) and the external test set (72.37% vs. 54.26%). When the synthetic-only training set was increased 10-fold, CLNA further improved F1 scores to 83.21% on the internal test set and 76.77% on the external test set. These findings suggest that CLNA can control the magnitude of sampled latent variation through a style parameter, thereby improving diversity in otoendoscopic text-to-image synthesis. CLNA-generated images could support downstream classifier training under reduced use of real images.

candidates.title: Exact autoregressive sampling of planar Ising spin glasses via the Kac--Ward theory
candidates.abstract: Abstract Independent samples from the Boltzmann distribution are valuable for estimating spin-glass observables and evaluating approximate sampling methods. Local Markov chain Monte Carlo methods typically generate temporally correlated samples and can encounter critical slowing down or metastable trapping, while neural autoregressive samplers such as variational autoregressive networks generate independent but approximate samples. Here we present an exact autoregressive sampling algorithm for planar Ising spin glasses based on the Kac--Ward theory. Under the chain-rule factorization, sequentially fixing spins induces boundary-localized external fields, which destroy the zero-field structure required for exact evaluation. By encoding these fields with a planarity-preserving auxiliary spin construction, the conditional partition functions are mapped to an extended zero-field Ising model and exactly evaluated using the Kac--Ward determinant formula. The method generates strictly independent and identically distributed samples with exact normalized likelihoods at a computational cost of $\mathcal{O}(N^{5/2})$ for $N$ spins, thereby providing an exact baseline for benchmarking neural autoregressive samplers.

candidates.title: Using Machine Learning to Compute Constrained Optimal Carbon Tax Rules
candidates.abstract: We develop a computational framework for deriving Pareto-improving and constrained optimal carbon tax rules in a stochastic overlapping generations (OLG) model with climate change. By integrating Deep Equilibrium Networks for fast policy evaluation and Gaussian process surrogate modeling with Bayesian active learning, the framework systematically locates optimal carbon tax schedules for heterogeneous agents exposed to climate risk. We apply our method to a 12-period OLG model in which exogenous shocks affect the carbon intensity of energy production, as well as the damage function. Constrained optimal carbon taxes consist of tax rates that are simple functions of observables and revenue-sharing rules that guarantee that the introduction of the taxes is Pareto improving. This reveals that a straightforward policy is highly effective: a Pareto-improving linear tax on cumulative emissions alone yields a 0.42% aggregate welfare gain in consumption-equivalent terms while adding further complexity to the tax provides only a marginal increase to 0.45%. The application demonstrates that the proposed approach produces scalable tools for macro-policy design in complex stochastic settings. Beyond climate economics, the framework offers a template for systematically analyzing welfare-improving policies in various heterogeneous-agent problems.

candidates.title: SynForge-Cardio: a unified multimodal synthetic dataset generation framework for privacy-preserving cardiovascular AI
candidates.abstract: Multimodal cardiovascular AI systems benefit from jointly available chest radiographs, 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs), and structured electronic health record (EHR) variables. In practice, multi-institutional model development is constrained by privacy regulations, institutional data silos, and class imbalance for less common findings. Existing open-source synthetic data tools are largely modality-specific: tabular libraries such as Synthetic Data Vault (SDV)/Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN), image generators based on latent diffusion, and time-series methods such as Time-series Generative Adversarial Network (TimeGAN) each require its own setup, configuration, and validation. This study presents SynForge-Cardio, a multimodality orchestration framework for prompt-driven synthetic dataset generation across chest X-ray (CXR), 12-lead ECG, and EHR modalities. Rather than introducing a new generative backbone, SynForge-Cardio coordinates established components—latent diffusion with optional low-rank adaptation for CXR; parametric and bounded morphology-preserving augmentation (with an optional TimeGAN path) for ECG; and size-aware routing among jitter augmentation, Gaussian copula, and CTGAN/Tabular Variational Autoencoder for EHR—behind a shared clinical prompt interface, a rule-based router, and a postgeneration quality/privacy reporting layer. The three modalities were generated independently from separate datasets; the framework does not perform patient-level joint synthesis and makes no claim of anatomical or physiological consistency across modalities. This system is implemented as a FastAPI backend with a React frontend and can run on a single workstation GPU. Herein, we formalize the orchestration objective, specify modality-wise models and metrics [Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), dynamic time warping (DTW), power spectral density similarity, Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics, correlation preservation, and distance-to-closest-record privacy screening], and describe an evaluation protocol on public corpora (NIH Chest X-ray14, PTB-XL, and the UCI Cleveland Heart Disease dataset), including a four-regime train-on-synthetic/test-on-real (TSTR) utility analysis with five random seeds. On the framework alone, we measured 94.6% modality-routing accuracy, 100% direct-vs.-routed generation equivalence on the evaluated cases, 59 unnecessary generator calls avoided, and 100% validation/reporting completeness (1,105/1,108 tests pass, 3 skipped). Downstream-utility results were mixed: augmenting a 25%-real training set with synthetic data changed the held-out AUROC by −0.041 to +0.050 across three CXR tasks (none significant at five seeds); by +0.019 for ECG MI-vs.-NORM [produced by mode B (bounded real-waveform augmentation, whose synthetic samples can be matched to their true source recording at top-1 ≈ 42.7–43.4%, and hence, mode B is not an independently learned generative model)]; and by +0.017 for EHR heart disease classification, which is not evidence of benefit given the 61-record hold-out set (the test-set bootstrap 95% CI for the difference includes zero). Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV acquisition was not completed because credentialed access was unavailable; all reported EHR results were UCI-based. SynForge-Cardio is intended as a practical, reproducible research framework for privacy-conscious cardiovascular data augmentation and prototype development.

candidates.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
candidates.abstract: We describe our solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge: 100 long-horizon household tasks in the OmniGibson simulator. We placed 9th on the final leaderboard, the only independent team in the top 10. The core of the solution is a single vision-language-action (VLA) model, one checkpoint for all 100 tasks, built on our 1st-place 2025 solution, which is based on $π_{0.5}$. On the 50 tasks shared with 2025, its Q rises from 0.260 to 0.371; across all 100 tasks it scores 0.392. Our main conclusion from 2025 was that the model was undertrained, so most of the 2026 work went into training the model for longer, optimizing some training parameters, making each training step slightly faster and reducing the gradient noise: a migration from 50 to 100 tasks (semantic stages built from the demonstrations' skill annotations, task and stage embeddings of new tasks warm-started from similar old ones, and a 21-dimensional action space matching the teleoperation controls); variance-reduced multi-sample flow matching with a simple noise-vs-compute model that picks the number of action-expert samples per observation without ablations; and a 200k-step training run, about one pass over the 211M frames of the demonstrations. A cloud evaluation infrastructure keeps a shared record with provenance, episode diagnostics and restorable simulator states, and runs six simulators on one GPU together faster than real time. On top of the learned policy, 14 tasks are routed to a GPT-6 Astra coding agent that controls the robot through observation and motion tools, starting every episode from a frozen copy of its own practice session on training instances. Across these 14 tasks, Astra's mean Q is 0.639, against 0.108 for the learned policy. The public submission included only part of the Astra results and scored 0.446 Q with 27.3% full-task success.

candidates.title: Data-driven multifidelity multiscale topology optimization via phasor-based evolutionary de-homogenization
candidates.abstract: Multiscale topology optimization is crucial for designing porous infill structures with high stiffness-to-weight ratios and excellent energy absorption. Although gradient-based methods provide a rigorous framework, they are computationally expensive and struggle to capture cross-scale sensitivities in nonlinear settings. Moreover, the resulting hierarchical geometries are often overly complex and lack macroscopically meaningful features. To overcome these issues, we propose an evolutionary de-homogenization framework that couples MultiFidelity Topology Design with a phasor-based de-homogenization technique. The framework translates low-dimensional geometric descriptors into explicit, CAD-compatible high-resolution structures through a hybrid evolutionary algorithm integrating NSGA-II selection, PCA-VAE-enabled latent-space crossover, and a novel image-deformation-based mutation operator. This gradient-free approach supports multi-objective refinement through non-differentiable geometry processing and body-fitted high-fidelity analysis. The numerical studies show design trade-offs for stiffness, stress, and buckling objectives; the intended scope is design-set exploration rather than universal computational superiority over full-scale gradient-based optimization.

candidates.title: A Charge-Consistent Long-Range Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential Compatible with Quantum Linear System Algorithms
candidates.abstract: Abstract Charge equilibration in machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) requires repeatedly solving linear systems, providing a promising target for quantum linear-system algorithms (QLSAs). However, conventional electronegativity equalization schemes suffer from spurious fractional charges between neutral fragments at large separations. To address this limitation, we incorporate atom-condensed Kohn–Sham density functional theory approximated to second order (ACKS2) into a long-range equivariant neural-network MLIP. Across benchmark systems, the ACKS2-based model improves energy, force, and charge predictions. At a molecule–metal interface, ACKS2 restores molecular fragments to near-neutral charge states upon separation while preserving local charge redistribution near adsorption. Because ACKS2 charge equilibration reduces to solving a linear system, the classical solver can be directly replaced with the Harrow–Hassidim–Lloyd algorithm during inference, demonstrating compatibility with quantum linear-system solvers. These results indicate that ACKS2 provides a promising framework for charge-aware MLIPs and highlight a potential pathway toward atomistic simulations based on QLSAs.

candidates.title: The Dose Makes the Poison: Exposure-Aware Evaluation of Generative Drug Design
candidates.abstract: Generative models are increasingly used to propose molecules for drug discovery. They can produce far more candidates than can be experimentally tested, making computational selection essential. Most selection methods rely on predicted molecular properties, such as potency and toxicity, but overlook how these properties translate into drug exposure at a given dose. As a result, molecules that appear promising on paper may require impractical doses or raise safety concerns. We investigate this gap by using physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulations to re-evaluate molecules selected from three PARP1-targeted generative pipelines. Of 60 shortlisted molecules, seven fail to achieve sufficient target exposure, while 28% of the remaining candidates show predicted safety risks at their required dose. Moreover, 85% of candidates with an achievable dose are outperformed by molecules overlooked during static selection. These findings suggest that accounting for dose and exposure can substantially change which generated molecules are considered promising for drug development.

candidates.title: Investigation and Optimization of Air Pollution Risk by a Multi-criteria Decision Making Method Using Fuzzy TOPSIS: A Case Study of Construction Workers
candidates.abstract: Background: Investigating human health during work importantly affect the safety and efficiency of the society. Different types of activity, including industrial, constructional, heavy duty ones, etc., affect the health of workers during their activities. In this study, the Multi-Objective Decision-Making (MODM) method was combined with fuzzy TOPSIS to investigate and optimize the air pollution risk affecting the health and safety of construction workers of Lar City, Fars Province, Iran. Methods: The comparison matrices (binary) and the Phillips–Perron test of different criteria and sub-criteria of health risk, including safety view, safety efficiency, understanding the risk, and risk investigation, were assessed to find the most influential factors for the optimization of the health risk of the workers. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. However, among the sub-criteria, the most effective ones were “worker knowledge”, “manager knowledge”, “logistic specialized managers”, “modern facilities”, and “modern technology”. The selection of the linear and non-linear models was conducted according to the F values, and the model parameters were estimated using the Newton-Raphson test. Most coefficients were significant at P= 0.99. The model also has a high describing value of 0.97. The final estimated homogeneity coefficient was equal to 1.31, and it ranged from 0.86 to 2.72 for the critical risk investigation. The significance of the present research is to increase the health and safety of workers during work resulting in a more sustainable and healthier environment. Conclusion: Accordingly, the managers could handle the risks, determine the tolerable risks, indicate the risk of each process to control expenses, and take the essential measures for optimization.

candidates.title: Probing the biomolecular design space with generative modeling
candidates.abstract: Discovering new-to-nature biomolecules requires navigating a design space that has only been sparsely explored. Traditional paradigms such as rational design, directed evolution, and high-throughput screening have enabled the development of many successful functional biomolecules, but are significantly limited when given an unseen target or novel function, where there is no starting point for design. Generative modeling offers a way to approximate the continuous manifold underlying observed biological data, enabling the sampling of new candidates beyond any finite dataset while remaining within the support of viable, functional biomolecules. Here, we outline recent progress in generative biomolecular design through an algorithmic lens, bridging theoretical foundations with its extensions and applications in truly de novo and controllable biomolecular design.

candidates.title: Fast Solution Methods for the Classical 0–1 Knapsack Problem
candidates.abstract: The classical 0--1 knapsack problem is among the simplest integer programs to state and among the most instructive problems for understanding why algorithm selection must follow instance structure. An input contains items with positive integer weights and profits, and the task is to choose a maximum-profit subset whose total weight does not exceed a capacity. The problem is weakly NP-hard, yet many large instances are solved quickly because exact algorithms exploit moderate numeric parameters, strong linear relaxations, dominance relations, or a small set of uncertain variables near the fractional break item. This review develops a theory-guided account of the principal fast solution methods for the classical problem. It proves the correctness and complexity of weight-indexed and profit-indexed dynamic programming, explains sparse Pareto-frontier implementations and reconstruction, derives the fractional-knapsack upper bound used by branch-and-bound methods, and establishes the correctness of meet-in-the-middle search. It then presents the core concept that underlies influential practical solvers and gives a detailed proof of the standard profit-scaling fully polynomial-time approximation scheme. Modern advances based on structured min-plus convolution are placed within this classical landscape rather than treated as isolated results. The central conclusion is that there is no universally fastest knapsack algorithm. Small item counts favor meet-in-the-middle search, moderate capacities or total profits favor dynamic programming, favorable density structure favors core-based exact methods, and very large numeric coefficients favor approximation. A final decision framework translates these theoretical distinctions into an implementable solver-selection policy while identifying open questions concerning adaptivity, certified switching among methods, memory efficiency, and realistic hard-instance generation.

candidates.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
candidates.abstract: Policy optimization is central to language model post-training, yet principled guidance remains limited. We revisit its theoretical foundations to identify algorithms that learn near-optimal policies using total samples and gradient steps governed by the base model's response coverage, a measure of how readily it generates optimal responses. We call such algorithms coverage-preserving. This guarantee captures the goal of amplifying capabilities accessible through sampling from the base model. (1) Coverage collapse. REINFORCE, the basis for PPO and GRPO, can drive the probability of optimal responses to near zero, even as reward improves. This coverage collapse stalls optimization, and convergence can require exponentially many steps despite good initial coverage. The failure arises even with exact gradients and persists under KL regularization to the base model. (2) Reference resets. We show that repeatedly resetting the KL reference to the most recent policy mitigates coverage collapse. We formalize this intervention in Approximate Policy Mirror Descent (APMD), a meta-algorithm that approximately solves a sequence of KL-regularized RL subproblems. APMD enables stronger regularization, making each subproblem easier to solve, while reference resets allow convergence to global optimality. (3) Coverage-preserving algorithms. For softmax linear policies over pretrained features, we use APMD to establish the first global convergence guarantees showing that widely used families of post-training algorithms are coverage-preserving. These include stylized PPO and GRPO variants with explicit KL regularization and reference resets, and squared-loss algorithms that implement them implicitly, including those used to train the Kimi models. These results clarify how regularization, clipping, and objective choice affect the sampling and optimization costs of post-training.

candidates.title: RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval
candidates.abstract: Cross-sensor remote sensing image retrieval aims to find scenes with the same content across heterogeneous sensors, such as SAR and optical or panchromatic (PAN) and multispectral (MS) imagery, without manual labels. Existing self-supervised methods either reconstruct sensor-specific pixel detail, align each image only with its co-registered twin, or rely on large transformers with 118-173M parameters (and up to 398M). We introduce RS-JEPA, a compact joint-embedding predictive framework built on a Vision Mamba encoder shared by both sensors. Since a state-space encoder reads an image as an ordered sequence of patches, we propose scan-path views, which treat two reading orders of the same image as two views with identical pixels and predict the hidden patches in one order from the visible patches in the other.To keep this prediction challenging, we propose Adversarial View Coupling (AVC), which learns the hardest split of the visible patches, and a neighbourhood consensus loss that aligns the scene similarities of both sensors. Extensive experiments on SAR-optical (BEN-14K, CBRSIR-VS) and PAN-MS (DSRSID) benchmarks demonstrate that RS-JEPA achieves the highest F1@5 among twelve re-implemented methods (72.92, 80.35 and 94.43) with a retrieval network of only 3.88M parameters (14.57M in training, 8-16times fewer than prior JEPA retrievers). Like prior methods, RS-JEPA trains on co-registered pairs. Our results highlight reading order as a source of self-supervised views. code: https://github.com/Tanishq251/RSJEPA.

candidates.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
candidates.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns. The scaffolds are removed at evaluation. We apply the same framework to ALFWorld, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation. When evaluated without scaffolds, students trained with AutoScaffold outperform those trained with the corresponding RL baselines in all four domains, with gains of 7.2 points in ALFWorld success and 4.0 points in average QA exact match. On GPU kernel generation, AutoScaffold increases the fraction of tasks with a correct kernel that runs faster than the PyTorch reference by up to 5.0 points. On math, our student surpasses QuestA's reported accuracy using approximately one-third as many student training steps. Analyses show that the teacher identifies a different failure in each task class and shifts its scaffolds from step-by-step workflows to targeted fixes as the student improves, and that its revised scaffolds help the student learn more than keeping the previous scaffold or using no scaffold.

candidates.title: Quantifying charger-related uncertainty in electrical mobility analysis of aerosols with MPSS-UQ 1.0
candidates.abstract: Charging probability is the greatest source of uncertainty in electrical mobility-based measurements of aerosol size distributions, but its influence on the results is rarely quantified and reported. In bipolar charging, the charge distribution is almost universally modeled using the Wiedensohler approximation, although it has been shown to deviate significantly from the true charge distribution under many measurement conditions. The charge distribution depends, among other factors, on the mobilities of the charger ions, which are typically not precisely known. Ignoring this uncertainty can lead to biased size distribution estimates and severe underestimation of their uncertainty. In this work, we quantify the uncertainty that imprecisely known charger ion mobilities introduce into the charged particle fractions, and then propagate this uncertainty into the estimates of the particle size distributions using a modular Bayesian approach, in which the ion mobilities are treated as nuisance parameters and marginalized over their plausible range. The inversion method, which is available as the open-source Python package MPSS-UQ, is implemented with particular emphasis on computational efficiency and tested with both synthetic and real mobility particle size spectrometer data. For a month-long field dataset, marginalizing over the uncertain ion mobilities widened the posterior credible intervals of the estimated size distributions on average by a factor of 2.4, with factors up to 10 in some size classes, compared to conditioning on fixed mobility values. The wider intervals provide a more realistic assessment of uncertainties in the inferred size distributions, and quantifying the structure of this uncertainty helps identify where improvements in the characterization of charger ion properties or in the measurement setup would be most effective.

candidates.title: Assessing the Accuracy of Bayesian-Optimized CGMD in Predicting Polymer Miscibility
candidates.abstract: Abstract Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) presents a computationally efficient alternative to all-atom (AA) simulations for modeling polymer systems, yet the accuracy of its predictions for emergent thermodynamic properties remains a challenge. This study builds upon our previous work, which introduced a Bayesian optimization framework for refining Martini3 force field, to validate the transferability of these optimized models to multi-component systems. We demonstrate that CG force fields, optimized against single-chain properties (density and radius of gyration), can qualitatively estimate the phase behavior of both homopolymer blends and diblock copolymer systems. Bayesian-optimized topologies for polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), polystyrene (PS), and poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) were evaluated through direct simulation of binary blend morphologies and a PMMA-PEO (poly(ethylene oxide)) diblock copolymer system. The framework successfully predicted macroscopic phase separation in the immiscible PS-PMMA system and miscibility in the PVDF-PMMA system, with resulting density profiles showing qualitative agreement with experimental observations. Flory–Huggins interaction parameters ( $$\chi $$ χ ) estimated from Hildebrand solubility parameters ( $$\delta $$ δ ) correctly rank relative miscibilities and align qualitatively with literature trends. Our results show that optimizing for fundamental properties such as density and radius of gyration (achieving <10% error) implicitly captures the necessary thermodynamic contributions to predict complex, multi-component phase behaviors. Validation of miscibility prediction across two canonical homopolymer blends, combined with efficient parameterization of a diblock copolymer architecture, provides compelling evidence that Bayesian-optimized coarse-grained molecular dynamics is a robust and predictive tool for polymer thermodynamics, effectively bridging the gap between computational efficiency and predictive fidelity in materials discovery.

candidates.title: SynthStrategy: Extracting and Formalizing Latent Strategic Insights from LLMs in Organic Chemistry
candidates.abstract: Abstract Modern computer-assisted synthesis planning (CASP) systems show promise at generating chemically valid reaction steps but struggle to incorporate strategic considerations such as convergent assembly, protecting-group minimization, and optimal ring-forming sequences. We introduce a methodology that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to distill synthetic knowledge into code. Our system analyzes synthesis routes and translates strategic principles into executable Python functions representing diverse strategic and tactical rules, such as strategic functional group interconversions, protecting strategies and ring construction features. We validate the use of LLM-as-a-judge in this domain, demonstrating their efficacy in evaluating synthesis-specific code generation. By formalizing this knowledge as verifiable code rather than simple heuristics, we create testable, interpretable representations of synthetic strategy. We release the complete codebase and the USPTO-ST data set─synthesis routes annotated with strategic tags. This framework unlocks a novel capability for CASP: natural language-based route retrieval, achieving 74.5% Top-3 accuracy on our benchmark. We further validate our library through temporal analysis of historical trends and chemically intuitive route clustering that offers more granular partitioning than common previous methods. This work bridges the tactical-strategic divide in CASP, enabling specification, search, and evaluation of routes by strategic criteria rather than structure alone.

candidates.title: Forward-Value Discretization: Faster Stochastic Diffusion Sampling Without High-Order Approximation
candidates.abstract: Stochastic diffusion samplers often require substantially more neural function evaluations (NFEs) than deterministic samplers to achieve comparable sample quality. Although higher-order discretization accelerates deterministic sampling, its benefits for stochastic sampling remains unclear. We establish matching upper and worst-case lower bounds showing that stochastic samplers with higher-order approximations remain first-order convergent, even with exact score functions. Thus, increasing the approximation order does not generally improve the convergence order. Motivated by this limitation, we introduce forward-value discretization, a training-free framework that evaluates the data/noise prediction model at a lookahead estimate constructed from previous predictions. For deterministic sampling, the resulting Forward DPMSolver (F-DPMSolver), improves sample quality at low NFE budgets through its DDIM-based variant, despite remaining first-order convergent. For stochastic sampling, we develop Forward DDPM (F-DDPM), which evaluates the model at a cleaner lookahead point adjusted for subsequent noise injection. This estimate reuses both the previous model prediction and the previously injected noise. Both variants admit first-order convergence guarantees with one model evaluation per iteration. Across CIFAR-10, ImageNet, FFHQ, and LSUN, F-DDPM consistently achieves lower FID than the evaluated stochastic baselines at matched NFE budgets. With 1.5 times as many NFEs as deterministic baselines, it achieves competitive sample quality, narrowing the practical efficiency gap between stochastic and deterministic sampling. Code is available at https://github.com/Na-Li66/F-DDPM.

candidates.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Janus Kinase (JAK) and Histone Deacetylase (HDAC) Dual Inhibitors for the Treatment of Psoriasis.
candidates.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory dermatosis featured by aberrant keratinocyte hyperproliferation and persistent cutaneous inflammatory infiltration, lacking curative small-molecule therapeutics. Dysregulated Janus kinase signal transducer and activator of transcription pathway (JAK/STAT) and histone deacetylase (HDAC)-dependent epigenetic signaling represented essential pathogenic axes driving psoriasis progression. Inspired by synergistic crosstalk between these two pathways and our previous work identifying anti-psoriatic JAK/HDAC dual inhibitors, a series of novel dual JAK/HDAC inhibitors were rationally designed and synthesized. Systematic enzymatic profiling revealed compound 11e exerted potent and balanced JAK2 and HDAC6 inhibitory activity (JAK2 IC50 = 2.1 nM, HDAC6 IC50 = 3.1 nM). Critically, topical cream formulation and oral administration of 11e dramatically alleviated erythema, scaling, and epidermal hyperplasia in the imiquimod-induced psoriasis mouse model. Collectively, compound 11e served as a promising lead compound for anti-psoriasis drug development, providing validated structural scaffolds for further optimization of next-generation JAK/HDAC dual inhibitors.

candidates.title: Cold Plasma-Engineered CNPs/TiO2 /CuO/Chitosan Nanocomposite for Cadmium Adsorption: Optimization, Isotherms, Kinetics, and Selectivity
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study reports the fabrication of a cold plasma–engineered CNPs/TiO 2 /CuO/Chitosan nanocomposite for effectively sequestering cadmium (Cd(II)) ions from aqueous media. The green cold-plasma synthesis approach simultaneously integrated multiple functional groups onto carbon nanoparticles (CNPs), generating a highly active heterogeneous surface. Applied to the ternary TiO 2 /CuO/Chitosan system, the nanocomposite delivered superior adsorption performance. Response surface methodology (RSM) optimized key process parameters: initial Cd(II) concentration at 68.62 mg L -1 , nanocomposite dosage at 26.20 mg, pH 6.89, and contact time of 79 min. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) confirmed the statistical significance of these variables and their interactions. Under these optimized conditions, the nanocomposite achieved a 91.98% adsorption efficiency. Kinetic analysis followed a pseudo-second-order mechanism, while isotherm data aligned well with the Freundlich model, suggesting multilayer adsorption. The nanocomposite’s selectivity in binary systems containing Pb(II) ions was also evaluated. In single-component systems, equilibrium capacities reached 120.45 mg g -1 and 99.75 mg g -1 for Cd(II) and Pb(II), respectively. In binary matrices, these capacities decreased to 85.65 mg g -1 and 50.35 mg g -1 , and the selectivity coefficient (αCd/Pb) peaked at 4.58 (pH 6.5). Reusability studies confirmed the nanocomposite’s structural and chemical stability, retaining 87.25% of its adsorption efficiency after five successive acidic desorption cycles. These findings demonstrate that the cold plasma-engineered CNPs/TiO 2 /CuO/Chitosan nanocomposite is a robust, efficient, and environmentally friendly candidate for sustainable wastewater treatment applications.
